examples.solution_text:
(a) $\angle ABC=90^{\circ}$ because the angle in a semicircle is a right angle.
$\begin{aligned}AC&=2\times6.5=13\text{ cm}\\BC^2&=AC^2-AB^2\\&=13^2-12^2\\&=25\\BC&=5\text{ cm}\end{aligned}$
(b) Again, $\angle ABC=90^{\circ}$.
$\begin{aligned}\angle BCA&=180^{\circ}-90^{\circ}-42^{\circ}\\&=48^{\circ}\end{aligned}$

The central angle and $\angle ACB$ stand on the same minor arc $AB$.
$\begin{aligned}\angle ACB&=\frac12\times\angle AOB\\&=\frac12\times104^{\circ}\\&=52^{\circ}\end{aligned}$

$C$, $D$ and $E$ lie on a straight line.
$\begin{aligned}\angle ADC&=180^{\circ}-72^{\circ}\\&=108^{\circ}\end{aligned}$
An exterior angle of a cyclic quadrilateral equals the opposite interior angle, so $\angle ABC=72^{\circ}$.
Opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral are supplementary.
$\begin{aligned}\angle BCD&=180^{\circ}-98^{\circ}\\&=82^{\circ}\end{aligned}$
The smaller central angle and $\angle ABC$ stand on the same arc $ADC$.
$\begin{aligned}\angle AOC&=2\times\angle ABC\\&=2\times72^{\circ}\\&=144^{\circ}\end{aligned}$

$\angle ABD$ and $\angle ACD$ stand on the same arc $AD$, so they are equal.
$\angle ACD=43^{\circ}$.
Equal chords are equidistant from the centre. Therefore $OF=OE=6.4\text{ cm}$.

$\angle ABC$ stands on the major arc $AC$, so use the reflex central angle.
$\begin{aligned}\text{Reflex }\angle AOC&=360^{\circ}-138^{\circ}\\&=222^{\circ}\end{aligned}$
The angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference standing on the same arc.
$\begin{aligned}\angle ABC&=\frac12\times222^{\circ}\\&=111^{\circ}\end{aligned}$
